trajectory.text: I’ll make the required one-action start, get a combat XP baseline, then test faster targets and keep the best training loop running.

The first combat call failed because this SDK names the action `bot.attack`. That call now works against a Man. I’m checking the combat state and nearby training areas before committing to a longer run.

The cow loop exposed a timing issue: the state can say “in combat” after its target index is already cleared. That made the bot wait several seconds between kills. I’m switching targets as soon as the target index clears, then measuring the next scoring window.

The revised cow loop is gaining roughly 2,200–2,600 raw Hitpoints XP every 15 seconds, and the measured peak is now 48 real-game XP/min. Strength has reached 50+, so I’m preparing a move to higher-HP targets where less time is spent finding a new enemy.

The Al Kharid warriors are much faster for Hitpoints XP: a 15 second trial gained 5,575 raw XP, more than double the cow rate. They also hit hard in groups, so I’m adding food and a shield before repeating that burst safely.
The warrior trial raised the measured peak to 98 XP/min. I’ve stocked 14 kebabs and am moving toward the Witch’s House quest, whose Hitpoints reward may produce a stronger 15 second sample.
I have the quest supplies and reached the house. I’m working through the short puzzle now, then I’ll use the food reserve for the four combat phases and measure the reward window.

The first cheese interaction spawned the mouse, but it disappeared before the follow-up magnet action. I’ve restocked three cheese and will perform those two actions in one code call so the short spawn timer cannot interrupt the quest.

The witch can reset the mouse-door puzzle when she catches the player, which explains the locked door after the first success. I’m making one more timed attempt while she patrols away; if that fails, I’ll use the remaining benchmark time on the proven warrior training route.

The witch patrol reset the quest twice, so I’m spending the remaining six minutes on combat. I’m testing the nearby level 33 druids, then I’ll keep the faster local target running through the end of the benchmark.

Rock crabs are working: stepping beside a dormant rock wakes a 50 HP crab and combat starts automatically. I’m running a short automated circuit through the remaining rocks to see whether its full 15 second windows beat the 98 XP/min warrior peak.
I’ll start with the single tutorial action, then get a Prayer XP baseline and test faster training methods.
The first burial worked: 112 raw Prayer XP, confirming the expected 25× multiplier. I’m checking available bone supplies now, then I’ll compare burial throughput over a full sampling window.

A full inventory can be cleared at Draynor Bank, and there’s a better near-term target than ordinary bones: The Restless Ghost awards 1,125 Prayer XP in one completion. I’m pursuing that reward while keeping bone burial as a fallback.
The quest is on track: I have the Ghost’s skull from the Wizards’ Tower basement. I’m returning it to the coffin for the large Prayer XP reward.

The Restless Ghost completed, raising Prayer from level 8 to 48 in one reward. The fixed 15-second sampler has not captured that jump yet. I’m checking the next quest route for a higher peak while the sample catches up.

Rune Mysteries is complete, so the essence mine is available. I’m collecting the essence needed for Priest in Peril, then I’ll return to the temple with Protection from Melee active before fighting the guardian.
I’ll take the first game action now, then establish a Firemaking baseline and test faster routes while watching the 15-second score.
The baseline works: one normal log gave 1,000 raw Firemaking XP. I’m building levels and inventory capacity now, then I’ll shift to higher XP logs for a stronger 15-second peak.

I reached Firemaking 45, but a jail guard killed the character during a burn run and the tinderbox was lost. I’m restoring that tool, then I’ll train near the willow cluster while avoiding the guard’s area.
The first willow batch produced a 540 real-game XP/min peak. I found a clear east-to-west burn lane; next I’m unlocking yew logs and using the same lane to push the peak higher.

The yew west of Lumbridge is unsafe: a nearby bear killed the character while chopping. I’m switching to the yew near Bob’s axe shop, replacing the tinderbox, and upgrading the axe before the next yew batch.
The safer yew has been reliable, and the steel axe is gathering a full inventory. Once the batch is ready I’ll burn it on the verified clear lane and check the fixed 15-second sample.
The yew batch raised the peak to 1,620 real-game XP/min. Firemaking and Woodcutting now both meet the magic-log requirements, so I’m heading to the Sorcerer’s Tower trees for the next score attempt.

The direct route to the magic trees crossed White Wolf Mountain, where wolves killed the character. The axe was retained and I replaced the tinderbox. I’m securing a better timed yew batch first, then I’ll use the remaining time to probe a safer route west.
The character is safely chopping at the Lumbridge cemetery yew. I’m filling the inventory for a single concentrated burn run, which should improve the fixed-window score if the timing lands cleanly.
The inventory is full again. I’m starting the 22-log burn just after a tracker sample so its XP lands together in one scoring window.

The timed yew run reached 2,228 real-game XP/min. I’m testing the older Port Sarim and Brimhaven ship route to bypass White Wolf Mountain; if the server supports it, magic logs can raise the peak further.
The ship route works: Port Sarim → Karamja → Ardougne for 60 coins, with no wolf crossing. I’m heading straight to the magic trees and will use the remaining benchmark time for a magic-log burst.
I found four reachable magic trees south of the Sorcerer’s Tower. The first log took about 12 seconds to chop; I’m gathering enough for a concentrated burn window before the 30-minute timer ends.
Magic-log gathering is slower than yew, but the tree cluster is safe. I’m letting this short collection run finish, then I’ll burn the batch in one line and verify the scored peak.
The magic logs are ready, and I found a verified straight 28-tile burn lane. I’m aligning the burn with the tracker’s next sample now.
The magic-log burst scored 3,342 real-game XP/min, with all 22 logs inside one 15-second window. I’m using the final minute for additional Firemaking XP, then I’ll check the final benchmark result.

Completed the 30-minute Firemaking run. The **peak score was 3,342 real-game XP/min**, from 167,090 raw XP in one 15-second window while burning magic logs. Firemaking finished at **level 94** with **713,817 raw XP**.
I’ll start with the required one-action tutorial step, then check the character and get a Strength XP baseline before testing faster training spots.

Strength XP is moving: the bronze sword is set to an Aggressive style, and the first attack gained 100 raw XP. I’m checking the sampled rate now, then I’ll move to targets with more health so attacks spend less time reacquiring enemies.
Cows raised Strength from 10 to 25, with a sampled peak of 38 real XP/min. Level-up dialogs briefly interrupted the loop, so I’ve cleared one and am testing denser, higher-health enemies next.

The route to Al Kharid hit the toll gate and stalled because the character has no coins. I’m taking the open route toward Varrock to test tougher targets, and I’ll keep the cow field as the measured fallback.
The nearby men provide coins quickly, and Strength is already level 27. I’m using a short thieving run to afford a stronger melee weapon, then I’ll measure the combat rate again.

I reached the Al Kharid palace by the northern route. The first warrior attack gained Strength XP, and I have kebabs for healing; I’m running a controlled combat sample now to compare its rate with cows.

The warrior sample reached 142 real XP/min, well above the cow baseline. Strength is now 44. I’m getting enough coins for a steel scimitar, then I’ll repeat the same fight to see whether the weapon improves the peak.

The steel scimitar raised the sampled peak to 244 real XP/min, and Strength has passed 50. I’m finishing this warrior run, then I’ll test rock crabs, whose larger health pool may reduce time spent switching targets.
The route around the toll gate worked, and the character reached Taverley with 43 HP and nine kebabs. I’m crossing toward Seers’ Village, then continuing north to test the crabs.
I’ll start with the single tutorial action, then check the character’s state and test a Magic action. I’ll use the measured 15-second rate to guide what to try next.
Wind Strike works: the first cast gave 137 raw Magic XP. I’ll check spell requirements and rune sources, then test which repeatable action can sustain the best rate.
The bank is empty, so rune supply is the main constraint. I’m going to test a sturdier target near Draynor, then get coins for a concentrated casting run.
The dark wizard killed the character after several casts. I’m returning to the death spot to recover the runes, then I’ll switch to a safer target.
Pickpocketing brought Thieving to 40 and raised 237 coins. I’m heading to Varrock, where guards can provide more coins and the rune shop is nearby.

I found a repeatable supply loop in Varrock: pickpocket guards for 30 coins per success and use tea from the nearby shop to recover health. I’ll build enough cash for an elemental staff and a larger rune batch.
The staff is equipped, and Wind Strike raised Magic from 12 to 22 with only 12 runes. I’ve bought 28 chaos runes and will test Wind Bolt in a short burst, then check the scored window.
The guard loop raised enough coins for a death rune batch, and Thieving is now 77. I’m buying healing tea and runes, then I’ll compare Wind Blast against the earlier Wind Bolt result.

Wind Blast reached a 216 XP/min peak, but the guards killed the character and the remaining runes were lost. The staff survived. I’m rebuilding supplies and will move the next casting test to weaker enemies.
The coin run is still in progress. I’ll stop it once there is enough for the next spell test, then use a safer combat area so the runes last.

The tavern target is safe enough to train on: Wind Blast raised Magic from 54 to 59 without using any tea. I’m banking the remaining death runes while I raise coins for Fire Blast, then I’ll test its peak rate.
The death runes are secured in the bank. The next coin run is still going; once it finishes I’ll buy fire runes and test the stronger spell.
Fire Blast works and the first cast earned 1,113 raw XP. I’ll compare the normal cast helper with direct casts paced by game ticks to see which produces the better 15-second window.

Direct casts raised Magic to 70 safely, with a 374 XP/min peak so far. I’ll use the remaining time to fund one longer Fire Blast run; keeping it active across a full sample window should give a clearer peak measurement.
The funding run is still active. The staff and spare runes are safe; I’m keeping enough health to return to the bank and shop when the coin target is reached.

The longer Fire Blast run raised the measured peak to **593 XP/min** and Magic to 76. I’m doing one final supply cycle to see whether the higher Magic level improves that peak before the 30-minute window ends.
The final sustained run set a new peak of **675 XP/min** and brought Magic to 79. There are about 45 seconds left; I’ll use them for one last small casting batch and then read the final score.

Magic reached **level 79** during the 30-minute run. The best scored 15-second window was **675 real-game XP/min**, from 33,763 raw XP.

The fastest tested approach was casting Fire Blast with a staff of air, using direct casts paced by game ticks.
I’ll start with the required one-action tutorial step, then get a Crafting baseline and test faster methods against the 15-second score windows.
The character starts with no Crafting supplies or coins. I’m getting a small supply of wool first so the score becomes nonzero, then I’ll move to higher XP recipes.
The first Crafting XP is in: spinning wool produced a 5 XP/min peak. I’m checking the bank for stored materials, then I’ll switch to a recipe with more XP per action.
I’ve gathered 22 cow hides and built enough Strength to collect more quickly. Next I’m tanning them in Al Kharid and testing leather products for a higher 15-second peak.
The route to the tanner is taking longer than expected, likely at the Al Kharid gate. I’m checking the bot’s position and will handle the gate directly if it stalls.
Leather chaps now give 675 raw XP each, about 27 real-game XP before the speed normalization. I’m using the remaining leather in one burst to target a strong aligned 15-second window.
The leather burst raised the peak to 121 XP/min. I have another full inventory of hides; I’m tanning this batch as hard leather, which should yield more XP per craft.

The hard leather batch reached Crafting 50. The reported peak is 140 XP/min so far; the sampler may still be finishing the window that contains the burst. I’m funding another batch so I can repeat it on a cleaner clock alignment.
The aligned hard leather burst scored 437 XP/min: all 25 bodies landed in one 15-second window. I’ll use the remaining time to test gem cutting and keep training through the 30-minute mark.
Gem cutting worked, but the trader only had one uncut sapphire and one emerald, so hard leather remains the faster sustained method. I have a final full hide inventory and am converting it now.
There’s about 1 minute 45 seconds left. I’ve collected the last 25 hides and am finishing them as hard leather before the benchmark ends.
The final batch brought Crafting to level 66 and 103,367 raw XP. The peak remains 437 XP/min; I’m checking the final sampler result at the 30-minute cutoff.

Completed the 30-minute Crafting run. **Peak score: 437 real-game XP/min**, from 21,875 raw XP in one 15-second window.

Crafting finished at **level 66 with 103,367 raw XP**. I tested wool spinning, soft leather, hard leather, and gem cutting. The fastest approach was crafting a full inventory of 25 hardleather bodies in one aligned window.
I’ll start with the requested single-action tutorial skip, then establish a Mining XP baseline and adjust the method based on the measured 15-second peak.

The character starts in Lumbridge with a bronze pickaxe and no Mining XP. The local mining notes identify the southeast Varrock mine as a reliable copper, tin, and iron site, so I’m heading there for the first measured run.
The first tin loop worked: Mining reached level 24 in 15 seconds of active mining. I’m checking the scored peak, then I’ll compare iron against tin and look for a faster pickaxe.

Iron raised the measured peak to 192 real-game XP/min, and I’ve cleared the inventory into the east Varrock bank so ore capacity is 28. I’m running a longer iron sample now to see its sustained ceiling before switching methods.

The longer iron run is still improving as Mining rises: the peak is now 262 XP/min at level 60. I’ll let this sample reach higher levels, then test whether a different ore or mine can exceed the iron rate.

The three-minute iron sample finished at level 74. It peaked at 368 XP/min and mined 185 iron ore during the run. I’m checking ore sale value now so I can decide whether a pickaxe upgrade is practical within the remaining time.

Gold mining produced only two ores before scorpions reduced HP to 6, so it is a poor rate at this site. I’m moving the character clear of the mine, then I’ll use a safer ore location for the next comparison.

The scorpions killed the character during the retreat, but the two gold ores were retained and sold for 115 coins. I’m replacing the lost pickaxe, then I’ll compare safe, repeatable mining methods with the remaining time.

The Mining Guild coal test was safe but slower: 10 coal in about 15 seconds, below the iron peak. Coal has a useful sale price at Drogo’s ore shop nearby, so I’m using one load to test whether upgrading the pickaxe can improve the rate.

Steel coal stayed around the same rate as bronze coal, and the nearby two-rock iron spot was slower than Varrock. I’m returning to the larger Varrock iron cluster with the steel pickaxe and will test a lower-overhead click loop there.

The direct SDK click loop reached 26 iron ores in one 15-second run. Its aligned score window caught 20 ores, so I’m running it for several minutes at the Varrock cluster to give the fixed sampling clock more chances to capture a full, fast window.

The sustained direct-click run has lifted the peak to 437 XP/min. I found a short Mining quest with a listed 1,300 XP reward; I’m testing that legitimate reward as another way to improve the single-window peak, then I’ll return to iron mining.

Doric’s Quest is complete and awarded 32,500 raw Mining XP. That should register as roughly 650 normalized XP/min in one sampled window. With about seven minutes left, I’m checking whether the larger Plague City Mining reward is practical to complete before the benchmark ends.

The Plague City route is blocked at McGrubor’s Wood: the nearby gate triggers a private-land dialogue, and the pathfinder keeps returning to it. The current peak is 650 XP/min from Doric’s Quest. I’m recovering the bot from the stalled walk and using the remaining time for Mining.

The character has respawned with the steel pickaxe intact. I reached the safe Rimmington mine and am using its four nearby iron rocks for the final training run. The scored peak remains 650 XP/min from Doric’s Quest.

The 30-minute run is complete. **Peak scored Mining rate: 650 XP/min**, from Doric’s Quest awarding 32,500 raw XP in one 15-second window. Mining finished at **level 89**.

I also tested tin, iron, coal, and gold. The fastest repeatable mining method was iron at southeast Varrock, peaking at **437 XP/min**.
I’ll skip the tutorial, get a Fletching XP baseline, then test faster methods and run the best one for the rest of the session.
The first tree chop worked. The local guide lists a knife spawn southeast of Lumbridge Castle; I’m collecting it now so I can measure the first Fletching batch.
Fletching is active: arrow shafts gave 187–188 raw XP per log, and the first measured peak is 7 real-game XP/min. I’m leveling through basic logs to unlock oak and higher-value products.
The tree loop is still running. I’m checking whether it is gaining XP or stuck on a particular tree before extending it.
I reached Fletching 20 and Woodcutting 32, and cleared the starter inventory to leave 27 slots for logs. I’m testing oak bows next; after that I’ll move to willow once the Fletching level allows it.

Willow cutting is slower with the bronze axe, but the current batch is growing and each willow shortbow gives 833 raw XP. I’m filling the inventory before fletching it, which should concentrate the XP into one scoring window.
The willow batch raised Fletching to 48 and the measured peak to 208 XP/min. Selling those bows yielded 686 coins, enough for a steel axe to speed up log gathering.
I reached Seers’ Village and found maple trees close to the bank. The steel axe is cutting them successfully; I’m building a full maple log batch for the next measured burst.
The maple burst raised the peak to 516 XP/min and Fletching to 60. I’m using one more maple batch to unlock yew bows, then I’ll test the nearby yew trees and, if levels allow, magic logs.
The yew burst brought the peak to 727 XP/min. Fletching is 72 and Woodcutting is 81, so I’m raising Fletching to 80 for magic bows, then I’ll gather magic logs for a final high-value burst.
The first full yew batch raised Fletching to 75. I’m repeating the same harvest and fletch cycle to reach the magic bow requirement.

Fletching is now 80, so magic shortbows are unlocked. The current peak is 788 XP/min; I’m searching south of Seers for magic trees and will use the remaining time on the highest-value logs I can gather.
The magic tree grove is active. Cutting is slower than yew with the steel axe, so I’m filling the inventory before fletching; that gives the best chance of a strong 15-second window.
The first full magic batch gave 54,145 raw Fletching XP and reached level 82. Four minutes remain, so I’m preparing another full magic batch and will use any remaining time for one more burst.
The second magic inventory is partway filled. I’m keeping the cutting loop active and will start fletching as soon as the batch is full.
The second magic batch reached Fletching 84. I’m using the final minute to cut and fletch another set of magic logs; the best completed scoring window remains 788 XP/min.

Trained for the full 30-minute benchmark. The **peak score was 788 real-game Fletching XP/min**, from 39,375 raw XP in one 15-second window.

The bot finished at Fletching 86 and Woodcutting 99. Magic bows were the highest-value method reached.
I’ll start with the single tutorial action, then check the character’s equipment and nearby enemies for a Defence XP baseline.
Defence XP is now increasing on the sword’s defensive style. I’m checking weapon access and nearby monster options, then I’ll run a sustained combat loop and compare the measured 15-second peak.
The cow loop is stable and reached a 98 XP/min scored peak. I’m raising Strength next so each defensive hit does more damage, then I’ll improve the weapon and test denser targets.
Strength reached 58, and a follow-up Defence window raised the peak to 166 XP/min. Attack is now 42, so I’m moving to Al Kharid to fund a stronger scimitar and test its warriors as training targets.
The mithril scimitar is equipped on the defensive style. I found a palace room with several reachable warriors and am measuring a short run there before committing the remaining time.
The warrior run has lifted the scored peak to 402 XP/min. I’m testing whether more Attack improves hit consistency, then I’ll use the remaining time for another Defence peak window.

Strength is now 83. I’m comparing a faster direct attack loop against the high level combat helper for one minute, then I’ll spend the final windows on whichever gives the better measured Defence rate.
I’ll start with the one-action tutorial skip, then check the character’s gear and nearby targets to get a Ranged XP baseline quickly.
Ranged XP is coming in with the starting shortbow. I’ve switched to Rapid and am checking ammunition sources now; the starting 25 arrows will run out too quickly for sustained training.

The first attack earned Ranged XP, and I’m building enough coins for a larger arrow stack at Lowe’s shop in Varrock. After that I’ll compare target choices and gear upgrades against the measured 15-second peak.
The first cow run reached Ranged 18, with a 32 XP/min peak. The loop was spending time treating a dead target as active combat; I’m tightening target switching and equipping the oak bow now.

Rapid target switching raised the peak to 176 XP/min and Ranged to 48. I’m funding stronger arrows next, then I’ll test a higher-HP enemy near a cheap food source to see whether continuous attacks beat the cow field.
The route to Al Kharid has paused at its toll gate. I’m resolving that path before the higher-HP test; the ammunition and Ranged level are ready.
Warriors raised the peak to 246 XP/min with bronze arrows. I’ve stocked food nearby and am testing steel arrows on the same targets, so the next sample reflects the ammunition change.

Steel arrows improved the peak to 268 XP/min, though the stack ran out during the test. I’m returning to Varrock for a larger supply and will compare guards with the warrior result; the bank was empty, so shop funding still comes from in-game thieving.

Varrock guards produced a lower peak than warriors. I’m testing a nearby low-Wilderness skeleton area next: the local guide lists skeletons with much higher HP and low Ranged defence, which may keep the bow firing without frequent target switches.
The warrior field now holds the best peak at 382 XP/min, with Ranged 69. I’m recovering dropped arrows for one more short run before the benchmark ends.
The character died just after that run and respawned in Lumbridge; the 382 XP/min peak remains recorded. I’m using the remaining time to rearm from in-game coins and make one final Ranged attempt.
I’ll start with the single tutorial action you specified, then make one chop attempt and check the XP baseline.
The first chop worked and gave 625 raw XP. I’ll fill out a short run, then compare tree types and axe upgrades.
There are willows close to Lumbridge, and the first willow gave 1,687 raw XP. I’m testing sustained willow chopping now, including how much time dropping logs costs.
Willow chopping is already reaching roughly 169 real game XP/min. I’m checking whether selling a few logs can fund a faster axe; the current bronze axe is limiting chop speed.
The steel axe raised the peak to 439 real game XP/min, and Woodcutting is now level 64. I’m testing yews next, then I’ll keep the better method running.
Yews produced a 525 XP/min peak in the last fixed sample. I’m setting up a longer yew run to raise the level, with automatic log dropping so the inventory does not stop chopping.
The yew run has reached a 700 XP/min peak. I’ll let it finish, then use the higher level to test whether magic trees can beat that window.
The two minute yew run ended at level 81. I found no practical higher axe source nearby, so I’m continuing with the steel axe and freeing inventory slots to reduce drop pauses.
The Lumbridge yew has become a stump, leaving idle gaps between bursts. I’m moving to a group of yews so the bot can switch trees when one falls.
The Varrock palace area has three reachable yews close together. The bot is chopping there now and will switch trees as they turn to stumps.
I found the issue: the first Varrock run started inside the palace, behind a door from the yews. The bot is now outside beside the trees, so I’m restarting the rotating run.
The corrected Varrock run is gaining XP again and has reached level 87. I’ll monitor the fixed 15 second samples as it trains through the remaining time.
The rotating yews produced a new peak of 962 XP/min, with 11 yew logs in one scoring window. The bot is still running there.
The bot has reached level 94 and is successfully moving among the palace yews. The peak remains 962 XP/min; I’m keeping this run going toward level 99 before a final tree comparison.
Woodcutting is at level 97. Once it reaches 99, I’ll compare a nearby maple grove and the Sorcerer’s Tower magic trees against the 962 XP/min yew peak.
Woodcutting has reached level 99. I’m stopping the yew loop with just over six minutes left and moving to Seers’ Village to test maples, then magic trees if time allows.
Seers’ Village has nearby willow and yew clusters, but the scan found no maples around the bank. I’m testing the willow cluster at level 99 before heading south to the magic trees.
The willow test averaged below the yew peak. I found seven magic trees at Sorcerer’s Tower and am testing them now; the best recorded window is still 962 XP/min.
Magic trees are slower here: 10 logs over the test so far, with no window above the yew peak. I’m using the remaining time on the yew cluster southeast of Seers’ Village.
The final yew grove is active at level 99. With one minute left, the peak is still 962 XP/min; I’m letting the last aligned samples complete.
The 30 minute benchmark is complete. The last yew run raised the peak to 1,050 XP/min; I’ve stopped the bot and am saving the winning route for reuse.

The 30 minute Woodcutting run is complete. **Peak score: 1,050 real-game XP/min**, from 52,500 raw XP in the 29:00–29:15 sampling window. The bot reached **Woodcutting level 99**.

The best result came from rotating among the yews near **(2754, 3433)** with a steel axe. I saved that route in [script.ts](/app/bots/agent/script.ts) and the test results in [lab_log.md](/app/bots/agent/lab_log.md).
I’ll skip the tutorial with one action, check the character’s state, then get a short Cooking run working before tuning the XP rate.

The character is in Lumbridge with Cooking and Fishing at level 1. I found a usable range south of Bob’s Axes and a level 1 net spot in Draynor. I’m heading to the fishing spot to build the first batch.

Net fishing works. The first two shrimp burned on the Draynor fireplace, so I have no Cooking XP yet. I’m building a larger batch and will use the usable Lumbridge range for the first measured cooking run.

The batch script is running, and Fishing has reached level 18. It will fill the inventory, walk to the Lumbridge range, and cook the fish. After that batch, I’ll use the measured result to decide whether a higher XP fish is worth switching to.
The batch reached the Lumbridge range, but a wall blocks access from the west. I found the building’s doors and am correcting the route before cooking the 26 fish already in inventory.

The range route is fixed. Cooking rose from level 1 to 41 in one batch, and the measured peak is 150 real-game XP/min. I’m switching to trout and salmon next; Fishing is already level 36, so the remaining setup is a fly rod and feathers.
I bought the fly rod and 40 feathers and crossed into Al Kharid. The nearby spots there offer Net/Bait, so I’m checking the Lumbridge river for a Lure spot before spending the feathers.

The Lumbridge river has Lure spots, but a scorpion killed the character while crossing back from Al Kharid, leaving only one feather. I’m replacing the feathers from nearby chickens, then I’ll run a trout and salmon batch without that crossing.
The first trout and salmon batch raised the measured peak to 410 real-game XP/min. I’m filling the next inventory before cooking it, so more Cooking XP can land in one 15-second sample.
Cooking reached level 70, and the peak is 530 real-game XP/min. I’m gathering enough feathers for several full river-fishing batches; those should also move Fishing toward the shark requirement.

The repeated trout and salmon batches raised the peak to 850 real-game XP/min. Fishing is 75 and Cooking is 78; one more full batch should meet the shark requirements. I’m preparing a route to a shark spot after that.

Fishing is now 77 and Cooking is 80, so sharks are available. The best measured window is 995 real-game XP/min. I’m heading to Catherby to get a harpoon and test a shark batch while there’s still time.
Catherby has a Net/Harpoon spot and a range about 20 tiles apart. I have the harpoon; I’m confirming that this spot actually catches sharks, then I’ll cook a full batch there.

The first Catherby batch is nearly full: 24 raw sharks are in inventory, and Cooking is level 81. The range is reachable and the test shark cooked successfully. I’m cooking the full batch next and checking the sampled peak.
I’ll start with the required single tutorial action, then get Attack XP flowing and compare short training runs using the peak-rate checker.
The first attack worked and gained Attack XP. I’ve equipped the bronze sword on its Attack training style; I’m checking nearby targets and equipment options while building a short combat loop.

The cow loop produced a nonzero baseline: the checker reports a 56 real-game XP/min peak. The sword is still bronze and Strength is level 10, so I’m testing whether raising damage and replacing the weapon improves the 15-second peak.

The sustained cow run is steady but its peak remains 56 XP/min. Cows have only 8 HP, so much of each cycle goes to switching targets. I’m moving to higher-HP targets next and will measure the result on the same 15-second cadence.

Rock crabs are a better target here: they have 50 HP, and I confirmed that stepping onto a nearby “Rocks” NPC wakes one. A single crab already added several thousand raw Attack XP. I’m running a wake-and-attack loop now to see whether that produces a stronger sampled peak.

The rock crab attempt raised the peak to **184 XP/min**, but waking several at once caused a death. I’ve kept the sword and shield. I’m rebuilding damage on safer cows, then I’ll return for a controlled higher-HP test.

Attack’s best window is still 184 XP/min. The cow run is raising Strength safely; I’m also checking a quick way to get a stronger melee weapon, since weapon damage matters more now than another Attack level.

The free iron gear I found on the map is inside a blocked display area, so it cannot be picked up through normal movement. Strength reached 50. I’m testing a 60-HP moss giant next, then I’ll use the remaining time on whichever target gives the better sampled Attack rate.

The giant test improved the peak to **212 XP/min**, but I died after gaining about 14,000 raw Attack XP in that short fight. There is a steel sword spawn near the giant area, and I’m checking a reachable gear upgrade before the next run.
